newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Petronas says no change in foreign contract terms.
newsitem.headline: Petronas says no change in foreign contract terms.

text.p: Malaysia's state oil company Petroliam Nasional Bhd said on Thursday it has no intention of revising the terms of its contracts with foreign oil companies, despite earlier indications it was willing to give more incentives.

"We said we would review it," Petronas President Hassan Marican told Reuters after announcing the company's financial results for the year ended March 31, 1996. "We have reviewed it and we're not going to change it."
The standard production sharing contract with foreign oil companies calls for an 80-20 split in Petronas' favour of all oil produced after costs are deducted.
Asked about complaints from some oil contractors that Petronas has dragged its feet in giving approvals for discovered fields to go into commercial production, Hassan said: "That's not true."
"Permission is never denied, once you declare a field is commercial, otherwise we could be sued."
